cases.description: A number selects for the value it equals before any category is asked for, though it is written after the category the value is in.
A number key is compared numerically, and the first of two equal keys wins.
A key the number test reads as a number is one, an exponent included.
A fraction is a number a key may be.
A negative number is a number a key may be.
A number key is compared with the value, not with the number as number would show it: 2 does not select for 1.999, whose category is taken at 2.
A key that is neither a number nor a category never selects: 1,000 and Infinity are not numbers, and twelve is not a category.
Where two options share a category, the first wins.
A category is compared exactly as written, so One is no category and the value in one takes the chain.
A number in a category the placeholder writes no option for selects nothing and takes the fallback chain.
other is a category and the inline default is none: a number in other with no other option takes the chain, where the payload's default outranks the inline one.
Where nothing is selected, the payload's own default outranks the message's, as for every selection.
An absent value takes the fallback chain before the modifier is asked, and nothing is reported.
An absent value takes the chain before the locale is tested, so it reports no missing locale.
A value that is not a number is an input the modifier cannot process: the chain, and failed-modifier.
Empty text is not a number, whatever the host converts it to.
Text that is only whitespace is not a number.
An infinity is not a number the modifier can take.
The test reads the whole value, so 12px is not a number.
Where no locale is available the result is the empty string, before a number that would have matched a key exactly is compared, and missing-locale is reported.
An empty locale is not available either.
A plural selection that declares no option is a message error: the chain, and missing-options against the message.
A plural selection declaring no option takes the chain as every message error does, before the locale is asked anything.
How the placeholder is written makes the error, so it is reported over an absent value too.
An option the selection passes over is never read, so the value no conversion describes that it names is never reported.
plural takes its category from the number as number would show it: at most two fraction digits by default, so 1.999 is asked of as 2.
A minimum number's props name shows a fraction, so 1 is shown as 1.0 and its English category is other.
In Czech 1 shown as 1,0 is many.
The implementation-configured defaults of number are read as its props are.
A wrapper's props of number are read as the call's are.
plural's own properties override number's of the same name.
plural's own properties override number's property by property: number's minimum stands beside plural's maximum.
plural's own properties, composed over every layer, override number's composed over every layer, so the call's plural overrides the wrapper's number.
plural's own minimum widens the default maximum, as number's does.
Of number's properties only the digit properties are read: its maximum is, so 1.04 is asked of as 1, and its style and grouping are not.
The significant digits number shows are read too.
The rule type is what plural is, whatever a layer names, so it asks for the cardinal rules.
A selection the host cannot make is an input the modifier cannot process: the chain, and failed-modifier, where a request the host made would have selected other.

In English ordinals 2 is two.
In English ordinals 3 is few.

In English ordinals 13 is other, though 3 is few.
In English ordinals 21 is one.
In English ordinals 22 is two.
In English ordinals 23 is few.
In English ordinals 111 is other.
In Swedish ordinals 2 is one.

cases.description: An integer written with a fractional zero is the integer.
A negative integer is taken as the ordinal rules take it.
An ordinal of a fraction names no position: the chain, and failed-modifier.
The integer test comes before a key is compared, so a fraction fails though a key equals it.
Empty text is not a number an ordinal can take either.
A fraction fails even where a locale's ordinal rules would give it a category.
ordinal reads the properties under its own name and nothing of number's — number's significant digit would have shown 22 as 20 — and its rule type is pinned.
A number selects for the value it equals before any category, under ordinal too.
An ordinal declaring no option is a message error.
ordinal tests the locale first as plural does.
